output.title: Spotting Phishing Emails — research brief
output.purpose: Establish an evidence base for a short awareness course on recognising, checking and reporting phishing emails.
output.audience: Office staff with everyday email use and no security specialism
exclusions: Technical email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) configuration

researchQuestions.question: What warning signs do authoritative agencies highlight for phishing emails?
How should an employee verify a suspicious message without taking risky actions?
What reporting behaviours do agencies recommend and why does fast reporting matter?

sourceHierarchy.rationale: National cyber-security agencies publish current, authoritative guidance.

jurisdictions: General (US and UK guidance used as reference)
safetyBoundaries: Do not instruct learners to open attachments or links to test them.

dossierPlan.title: Warning signs of phishing
dossierPlan.notes: Focus on signs a non-specialist can check.

evidenceRequirements: Every claim cites at least one authoritative source.
currentnessRequirements: Record the access date of every web source.
